indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.1.2.1 Recognise materials as important resources for providing human needs
indicator.objective: Classify everyday materials based on their properties (soft, hard, rough, smooth, opaque, transparent and bendable)

skills.description: Name the properties of materials: soft, hard, rough, smooth, opaque, transparent, bendable.
Identify materials as soft or hard, rough or smooth.
Identify materials as transparent (see-through) or opaque (not see-through).
Identify materials as bendable or not bendable.
Sort everyday materials (cotton wool, wood, plastic, glass, paper, raffia) based on a given property.
Explain simply why a material is chosen for a particular use because of its property (e.g. clay for pots because it can be moulded; raffia for baskets because it bends easily).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Any material can be used for any purpose.

questions.stem: Which of these is a property of a material?
hints: Properties describe how a material feels or behaves.
Can you bend it?
questions.explanation: Bendable is a property of a material. It describes whether the material can be bent without breaking.
questions.misconception: Any word can describe a material.

questions.stem: Which material is soft?
hints: Which one feels gentle to touch?
You can squeeze it easily.
questions.explanation: Cotton wool is soft. Iron nails, stones and wood are hard.

questions.stem: Which material is transparent?
hints: Which one can you see through?
Windows are made of it.
questions.explanation: Clear glass is transparent because you can see through it. Wood, metal and cardboard are opaque.

questions.stem: Which material is bendable?
hints: Which one can you bend without breaking?
Think of a rubber band.
questions.explanation: Rubber is bendable. Glass, stone and iron are not easily bendable and may break if forced.

questions.stem: What do we call a material that you cannot see through?
hints: The opposite of transparent.
Wood is an example.
questions.explanation: A material you cannot see through is called opaque.

questions.stem: A pupil is sorting materials into 'hard' and 'soft'. Which group is correct?
options: Hard: stone, iron; Soft: cotton wool, sponge
Hard: sponge, cotton wool; Soft: stone, iron
Hard: sponge, stone; Soft: iron, cotton wool
Hard: cotton wool, iron; Soft: stone, sponge
hints: Which materials cannot be easily squeezed?
Stones and iron are hard.
questions.explanation: Stone and iron are hard materials. Cotton wool and sponge are soft materials.

questions.stem: Ama touches a piece of sandpaper and a piece of glass. Which statement correctly describes their textures?
options: Sandpaper is smooth, glass is rough
Sandpaper is rough, glass is smooth
hints: Sandpaper feels bumpy.
Glass feels flat and even.
questions.explanation: Sandpaper is rough because it has a bumpy surface. Glass is smooth because it has an even surface.

questions.stem: Which set contains only transparent materials?
options: Clear plastic, clear glass, clean water
hints: Which materials can you see through?
Clear things are transparent.
questions.explanation: Clear plastic, clear glass and clean water are transparent materials. You can see through them.

questions.stem: Which of these materials is NOT bendable?
hints: Which one will snap if you try to bend it?
It is a hard metal.
questions.explanation: An iron nail is not bendable. It is a hard metal. Clay, rubber bands and raffia can be bent or moulded.

questions.stem: Why is clay used for making pots?
options: Because it can be moulded when wet and becomes hard when baked
hints: Pots are shaped by hand.
Clay can be shaped when wet.
questions.explanation: Clay is used for pots because it can be moulded into shape when wet and becomes hard when baked.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used for any purpose.

questions.stem: Which material is best for making a window pane?
options: Clear glass because it is transparent
Cotton wool because it is soft
hints: You need to see through a window.
Transparent materials let light in.
questions.explanation: Clear glass is best for a window pane because it is transparent and lets light through.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used for any purpose.

questions.stem: Why is raffia palm used for making baskets?
answer: because it is bendable and can be woven easily
it bends easily so it can be woven into baskets
it is flexible and easy to weave
hints: How are baskets made?
The material needs to bend.
questions.explanation: Raffia palm is used for baskets because it is bendable and can be woven easily.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used for baskets.

questions.stem: Name three properties of materials.
hints: Think about how materials feel.
Think about whether you can see through them or bend them.
questions.explanation: Properties of materials include soft, hard, rough, smooth, opaque, transparent and bendable.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'All plastics are transparent.' Is the pupil correct?
options: No, some plastics are opaque, like black plastic bowls
hints: Think about a black plastic bucket.
Can you see through it?
questions.explanation: Not all plastics are transparent. Some plastics are opaque, like black plastic bowls or buckets.

questions.stem: Why are cooking pots usually made of metal rather than cloth?
options: Metal is soft and cloth is hard
Metal is hard and can withstand heat, while cloth burns
Cloth is bendable and metal is not
Metal is transparent and cloth is opaque
hints: Pots go on a fire.
Which material can handle heat?
questions.explanation: Metal is hard and can withstand the high heat of cooking. Cloth is soft and would burn on a fire.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used for any purpose.

questions.stem: Sort these materials into 'transparent' and 'opaque': clear glass, wood, clear plastic, cardboard.
answer: transparent: clear glass and clear plastic; opaque: wood and cardboard
transparent: clear glass, clear plastic; opaque: wood, cardboard
clear glass and clear plastic are transparent; wood and cardboard are opaque
hints: Which ones can you see through?
Wood and cardboard are not see-through.
questions.explanation: Clear glass and clear plastic are transparent because you can see through them. Wood and cardboard are opaque because you cannot see through them.
questions.misconception: All materials are either completely transparent or completely opaque.

questions.stem: Why is cotton wool used for making pillows?
answer: because it is soft and comfortable to rest on
it is soft and makes the pillow comfortable
cotton wool is soft, so it is good for pillows
hints: What makes a pillow comfortable?
You rest your head on it.
questions.explanation: Cotton wool is used for pillows because it is soft and comfortable.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used for pillows.

questions.stem: Name one material that is bendable and one that is not bendable.
answer: bendable: rubber band; not bendable: iron nail
hints: Think of something you can bend.
Think of something that would break if you tried to bend it.
questions.explanation: Rubber and raffia are bendable. Glass, iron and stone are not bendable.

questions.stem: Design a simple raincoat for a farmer in Ghana. Choose a material that is suitable. Draw your design and write one sentence explaining why you chose that material.

criteria.description: Drew a simple design of a raincoat
Chose a suitable material (e.g. plastic, waterproof fabric)
Explained that the material is waterproof/does not let water through

hints: What happens when rain falls on the farmer?
The material should keep water out.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used for a raincoat.

questions.stem: A learner needs a material to make a transparent container to store water. Which material is best and why?
options: Wood, because it is hard and strong
Clear plastic, because it is transparent and does not let water through
Cotton wool, because it is soft
Rough stone, because it is heavy
hints: The container needs to be see-through.
It must hold water without leaking.
questions.explanation: Clear plastic is best because it is transparent (you can see through it) and it does not let water pass through.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used for any purpose.
